name: Mobutu Sese Seko
summary: Army chief who seized power in a 1965 coup and ruled Congo-Kinshasa, renamed Zaire in 1971, for 32 years through a single party, the MPR, and a presidency with near-total powers. His doctrine of "authenticity" rejected both capitalism and communism and promoted African cultural nationalism. At the UN he denounced colonialism, apartheid and the world economic order. He allowed multiparty politics only under pressure in 1990.
